howDoI.q: How do I warn the player before the wind blows?
How do I make wind that blows for a while and then stops?
How do I lift the player up to a high ledge?
How do I show the wind with a windsock?
How do I make wind that pushes sideways?
How do I make a place the wind does not reach?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Gusts is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and nothing in it can cost a life.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score.

The wind here comes and goes. Slippery and Bouncy shows wind that always blows. In this one a gust is calm, then flutters (the warning), then blows, then is calm again, round and round.

pages.head: Level 1: Wait for the Gust
pages.html:
Level 1: Wait for the Gust

A stone ledge is too high to jump to. Beside the first signs is a shaft of air standing on a stone slot in the ground. For about five and a half seconds it is calm. Then the leaves in it flutter for two seconds, with little gold shake marks, and then a gust blows up the shaft for three seconds, with long white streaks, and lifts Kit up through the ledge. When the wind drops he lands on the ledge.

The first sign says the leaves flutter first. The second says to wait in the shaft. Try a jump while it is calm and you will see why. There are six coins: two on the ground and four on the ledge, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A gust is a ring of three blocks. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor and pick up.calm. Its Next block is up.flutter and its Time is 100 ticks. up.flutter lasts 36 and turns into up.gust, which lasts 54 and turns back into up.calm. Because the last block points back to the first, the wind goes round for ever. There are 18.2 ticks in a second.
  • The wind is a pull. up.gust has its Gravity set to up and nothing else, so anyone standing in it is pulled up. up.calm and up.flutter pull down, like the sky, so the warning does not move Kit.
  • The warning is a block. up.flutter is the same as up.calm with leaves and shake marks drawn on it. It is a different shape from the gust, so a player who cannot tell the colors apart can still tell a flutter from a calm.
  • One shaft, many cells. The shaft is six cells high and three wide, all the same block, so every cell changes on the same tick. Every block of one kind changes together.
  • The ledge is a plank. A plank is solid on top only, so the gust lifts him up through it and he lands on it when the wind drops.
  • The slot. slot is a solid block in the ground under the shaft, so a player can see where the wind comes from.
  • The clock starts with the level. Every timer is set when the scene loads, which is why a level card comes first.
  • The walls. A hedge closes the room in at both ends.

pages.head: Level 2: Windsocks and Shelter
pages.html:
Level 2: Windsocks and Shelter

A tunnel runs through a hill. Gusts blow left along it, against Kit, and push him back out. Three windsocks stand on the hill. A sock droops when it is calm, twitches half lifted when the wind is about to blow, and streams out to the left in a gust. They change on the very same ticks as the wind in the tunnel, so they tell you from anywhere.

Two little shelters sit in the tunnel, with an awning and a lantern. There is no wind in a shelter. The first sign says the windsock shows the wind. The second says to wait in a shelter while it blows. Cross a stretch while it is calm, and wait in a shelter for each gust. Try walking into a gust and you will find out why. There are four coins, on the rugs in the shelters.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The tunnel wind is a ring. Open two.bbl. side.calm lasts 100 ticks and turns into side.flutter, which lasts 36 and turns into side.gust, which lasts 54 and turns back. side.gust has its Gravity set to left and down, so it pushes Kit left, and he still falls if he jumps.
  • The windsocks are in step. sock.calm, sock.flutter and sock.gust form a second ring with the very same times. Both rings start when the scene loads and change by the same lengths, so they never drift apart. A windsock has no pull; it is only a picture that changes.
  • The sock has a pole. The pole is its own block, pole, under the top block that changes.
  • A shelter is a gap in the wind. In each shelter, the cells where the tunnel wind would be are other blocks that pull down like the sky: awning, lantern, back, rug and rugCoin. Whichever block he is standing in decides his pull, so in a shelter there is none.
  • Coins on the rug. rugCoin adds 10 points and its Touched block is rug, so the coin goes and the rug stays.
  • A roof you can see. The tunnel has a stone roof and floor, so he cannot jump over the wind, and the ends are open: nothing here is invisible.
  • The walls. A hedge closes the room in at both ends.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A gust in Game-Maker is a block that pulls, in a ring that changes on a timer. Some things you may expect are not there:

  • It cannot make a random gust. A ring has fixed times, so the wind comes round every 190 ticks, the same each time.
  • It cannot start a gust when the player does something. Every timer starts when the scene loads, so the wind cannot rise because Kit stepped in the shaft.
  • It cannot blow harder in one place. A pull is on or off; how long Kit is in it makes him go faster, up to a top speed.
  • It cannot tell a block where the player is. A shelter works only because it is made of other blocks, not because anything shields him.
  • It cannot play a sound when a block changes. The warning has to be something you can see.
  • A windsock cannot feel the wind. It agrees with the wind only because its times are the same, so change both together.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.bbl, change up.gust's Time from 54 to 24. The gust is shorter and may let go before Kit reaches the ledge.
  • Change up.flutter's Time from 36 to 72 for a longer warning, or to 8 for a very short one.
  • In two.bbl, change a time in side and the same one in sock, or the socks will drift from the wind.
  • Open side.gust and set its Gravity to right and down, and the wind pushes him on instead of back.
  • Draw your own windsock in the blocks editor.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
